items.title: Remember: Ask what faithfulness looks like now
items.body: Read Psalm 94:19 and choose one short idea from the passage to remember without copying verse text. Write the idea in your own words, set a cue to revisit it later today, and when you return, note what changed in your thinking or actions. Close with one sentence of gratitude or one clear request to God.

items.title: Obey: Bring the wrong into the light
items.body: Read Psalm 32:5. Name the wrong plainly before God instead of softening it or punishing yourself for it. If another person was harmed, identify one honest step of confession, restitution, or repair that is safe and appropriate. Receive forgiveness as grace, then take that concrete step without using shame as a substitute for repentance.

items.title: Obey: Reject the label that shame assigns
items.body: Read Isaiah 54:4. Write down the label shame keeps attaching to you, then separate that label from what actually needs confession, healing, or growth. Choose one action today that treats you as a person still worthy of honest care before God: ask for help, return to community, or complete one responsibility without hiding.

items.title: Obey: Stay when you feel nothing
items.body: Read John 15:4. Do not use strong feelings as the test of whether abiding is real. Keep one simple rhythm for the next day: return to the passage, pray one honest sentence, and remain available to God even if the moment feels ordinary. Faithfulness during dryness is still faithfulness.

items.title: Obey: Change the conditions before temptation returns
items.body: Read Matthew 26:41. Identify the place, time, device, conversation, or emotion that usually lowers your resistance. Change one condition before the next vulnerable moment: remove access, leave earlier, add accountability, or prepare a different response. Then pray specifically for alertness and strength rather than relying on willpower alone.

items.title: Obey: Let joy become gratitude, not self-importance
items.body: Read Luke 10:20. Enjoy what is good without making success, attention, or momentum the center of your identity. Name the gift, thank God for it, and choose one way to share the good without turning the moment into a performance. Let celebration make you more generous and grounded.

items.title: Obey: Make love concrete in one relationship
items.body: Read 1 Corinthians 13:4-5. Choose one relationship where love needs a visible form today. Pick one quality from the passage—patience, kindness, humility, or refusing self-seeking—and turn it into a specific action: listen without interrupting, serve without announcing it, apologize, or give someone unhurried attention.
